name: Traceability Matrix - INF
rows: Infrastructure governance, risk appetite and reporting
The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
Establishes the risk appetite that must govern infrastructure design, procurement, cloud onboarding, network exposure and asset disposal decisions.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Governance, risk appetite and infrastructure security accountability
NDIA must manage infrastructure risks within approved security risk tolerance and document residual risks, exceptions and treatment decisions in relevant security and infrastructure plans.
Infrastructure governance, risk appetite and reporting
A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
Ensures accountable ownership for hardware, network and cloud security risks, including risks shared with providers.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Governance, risk appetite and infrastructure security accountability
Each material infrastructure risk or risk category must have an assigned risk steward responsible for treatment, monitoring, escalation and provider/shared-risk coordination.
Infrastructure governance, risk appetite and reporting
The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
Prevents NDIA infrastructure risk decisions from adversely affecting other Commonwealth entities, partners or shared services.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Governance, risk appetite and infrastructure security accountability

Infrastructure changes, interconnections, shared services and provider arrangements must consider downstream security impacts on other entities and share relevant risk information through approved channels.
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit

The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
Infrastructure procurement and outsourcing directly shape NDIA security posture and must not introduce unacceptable supply chain or service risks.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Procurement, supplier assurance and supply chain integrity

Procurement of hardware, network, cloud and managed infrastructure services must include security risk assessment, minimum security requirements and documented approval of residual supplier risk before engagement.
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit

Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
Mandatory PSPF flow-down requirements are needed in contracts for infrastructure suppliers, cloud providers, network carriers and subcontractors.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Procurement, supplier assurance and supply chain integrity

Contracts and procurement artefacts must include proportionate security clauses, PSPF/ISM obligations, right-to-assess/audit provisions, incident reporting, data handling, subcontractor controls and secure disposal/exit requirements.
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit
Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
Assures PSPF obligations are implemented by vendors operating or supporting NDIA infrastructure.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Contract security, provider monitoring and exit
NDIA contract owners must verify that infrastructure service providers, contractors and subcontractors implement the security controls and PSPF requirements specified by NDIA.
Supplier, privacy, fraud, cyber extortion and reporting response

Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
Security incident reporting from suppliers is essential to detect, contain and recover from infrastructure compromise.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Contract security, provider monitoring and exit

Infrastructure contracts must require prompt notification of actual or suspected security incidents and require providers to follow NDIA directions during investigation, containment, remediation and evidence preservation.
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit
Government entities providing outsourced services provide IRAP assessment reports to the government entities consuming, or looking to consume, their services.
IRAP reports enable NDIA to assess outsourced government services and cloud/platform services before use.
Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage and outsourced network/hosting services; conditional where NDIA provides services to other entities.
Procurement, supplier assurance and supply chain integrity

When consuming or providing outsourced infrastructure services, NDIA must obtain and consider current IRAP assessment reports for relevant services and use findings in authorisation and risk decisions.
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit

Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
Ongoing monitoring ensures contracted infrastructure controls remain effective across the contract life.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Contract security, provider monitoring and exit
Contracted infrastructure services must be monitored and reviewed against security terms, agreed controls, service levels, incident obligations and subcontractor commitments throughout the contract.
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit
Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
Secure transition and termination provisions prevent loss, unauthorised retention or insecure disposal of NDIA data and assets.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Contract security, provider monitoring and exit

Contracts must include completion/termination security arrangements covering data return or destruction, access removal, asset return, sanitisation, transition support, evidence of disposal and continuing confidentiality obligations.
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit
Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
Foreign ownership, control or influence can affect trustworthiness and availability of infrastructure suppliers, products and managed services.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Procurement, supplier assurance and supply chain integrity

Before engaging or renewing providers, NDIA must assess foreign ownership, control or influence risks for technology assets and services, manage changes during the contract and escalate/report material risks.
PSPF Direction 001-2024 - Managing Foreign Ownership, Control or Influence Risks to Technology Assets
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit
Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
Supplier security risks change over time and must be reassessed for continuing suitability.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Contract security, provider monitoring and exit

Infrastructure supplier risks must be reassessed during procurement, transition, operation, renewal, major change and exit, with treatments adjusted when threat, ownership, service or subcontracting arrangements change.
Supplier risk, FOCI, security clauses, monitoring and exit
Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
Use of secure, verifiable providers reduces compromise, supply chain and data sovereignty risk.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas through procurement, managed services, providers and subcontractors.
Procurement, supplier assurance and supply chain integrity

NDIA must use secure and verifiable vendors, providers and partners for hardware, network, cloud and associated infrastructure services; any unavoidable exceptions require documented residual risk treatment and CISO approval.
Continuity, logging, vulnerability disclosure and ASD threat engagement
A business continuity plan is developed, implemented and maintained to respond effectively and minimise the impacts of significant business disruptions to the entity's critical services and assets.
Infrastructure supports critical NDIA services; continuity planning is needed to minimise disruption from outages, cyber incidents or provider failures.
Directly applicable - Networks and Cloud Compute and Storage; Hardware Portfolio where assets support critical services.
Infrastructure resilience, continuity and emergency arrangements

NDIA must maintain business continuity plans covering critical infrastructure services, dependencies, recovery priorities, alternative connectivity/hosting options and restoration of hardware, network and cloud services.
Continuity, logging, vulnerability disclosure and ASD threat engagement
Plans for managing a broad range of emergencies are integrated within the business continuity plan.
Emergency arrangements must be integrated so infrastructure recovery works during cyber, physical, supplier and environmental events.
Directly applicable - all three scope areas where disruption affects NDIA critical services or assets.
Infrastructure resilience, continuity and emergency arrangements

Infrastructure continuity procedures must be integrated with emergency and crisis plans, including roles, communications, access arrangements and provider escalation for network, cloud and hardware incidents.
Classification, protective marking, privacy governance and approved data flows
The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
Infrastructure controls must protect OFFICIAL and security classified information stored, processed or communicated by NDIA systems.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Information classification, protective marking and infrastructure handling
NDIA infrastructure must implement handling, access, storage, transmission, backup and monitoring controls commensurate with the classification and sensitivity of information held or transmitted.
Classification, protective marking, privacy governance and approved data flows
The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
Security caveats impose special handling requirements that must be reflected in systems and infrastructure.
Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure stores, processes or communicates security classified or caveated information.
Information classification, protective marking and infrastructure handling
Infrastructure supporting caveated information must enforce applicable caveat handling requirements, including access restriction, segregation, logging and approved storage/transmission arrangements.
Classification, protective marking, privacy governance and approved data flows

The Australian Government Email Protective Marking Standard is applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information exchanged by email in and between Australian Government entities, including other authorised parties.
Email protective marking relies on supporting technology controls, gateways and records integrations.
Directly applicable - Networks and Cloud/SaaS email services; Hardware Portfolio where endpoint/email clients are managed.
Information classification, protective marking and infrastructure handling
Network, cloud email and endpoint infrastructure must support Australian Government email protective markings for messages exchanged with other Australian Government entities and authorised parties.
Classification, protective marking, privacy governance and approved data flows

The Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Security Classification' property (and where relevant, the 'Security Caveat' property) is applied to protectively mark information on technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information.
Metadata marking supports technical enforcement of classification-based access, retention and handling.
Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage and systems storing classified information; Networks where metadata travels across services.
Information classification, protective marking and infrastructure handling

Systems that store, process or communicate security classified information must apply the Recordkeeping Metadata Standard security classification and caveat properties to enable protective marking and control enforcement.
Classification, protective marking, privacy governance and approved data flows
Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
Rights metadata supports restrictions on access to information content in infrastructure systems.
Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage repositories and platforms where access restrictions are recorded or enforced.
Information classification, protective marking and infrastructure handling
Where NDIA categorises information by access restrictions, infrastructure platforms must capture and preserve appropriate 'Rights' metadata and use it to inform access control and handling.
Classification, protective marking, privacy governance and approved data flows
Entity implements operational controls for its information holdings that are proportional to their value, importance and sensitivity.
Infrastructure operational controls must scale with the value, importance and sensitivity of NDIA information holdings.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Information classification, protective marking and infrastructure handling

Infrastructure controls for systems, repositories, backups and networks must be proportionate to the business impact level, classification, sensitivity and criticality of the information holdings they support.
Commonwealth records, legal holds, retrieval, decommissioning and media sanitisation

OFFICIAL and security classified information is disposed of securely in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements, ISM, the Records Authorities, a Normal Administrative Practice and the Archives Act 1983.
Infrastructure policy must ensure OFFICIAL and classified information is securely disposed from hardware, media, backups and cloud storage.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and Cloud Compute and Storage; Networks where logs or configurations contain NDIA information.
Secure information, media and technology asset disposal
NDIA must dispose of information on hardware assets, removable media, backups, logs and cloud storage using approved retention, sanitisation, destruction and evidence requirements.
Commonwealth records, legal holds, retrieval, decommissioning and media sanitisation

Security classified information is appropriately destroyed in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements when it has passed the minimum retention requirements or reaches authorised destruction dates.
Classified information destruction requirements must be enforced for classified storage media and cloud repositories.
Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure stores, processes or communicates security classified or caveated information.
Secure information, media and technology asset disposal
Security classified information must not be destroyed before retention requirements are met and must be destroyed using approved handling and destruction processes with evidence retained.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
Core mandatory control for applying ISM principles through the full infrastructure lifecycle.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset register
NDIA must apply ASD ISM cyber security principles from planning and procurement through deployment, operation, change, maintenance and disposal of hardware, network and cloud infrastructure.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
Ensures ISM controls and guidance are selected and implemented according to risk for infrastructure systems.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset register
NDIA must select, implement and maintain applicable ISM controls for infrastructure systems using a documented risk-based approach and compensating controls where full implementation is not feasible.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology

The Authorising Officer authorises each technology system to operate based on the acceptance of the residual security risks associated with its operation before that system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
Technology systems must not operate with government information until residual risks are authorised.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset register
Each infrastructure technology system must be authorised by the Authorising Officer before processing, storing or communicating NDIA/government information, based on accepted residual security risk.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology
Decisions to authorise (or reauthorise) a new technology system or make changes to an existing technology system are based on the ISM's risk-based approach to cyber security.
Authorisation and change decisions must follow ISM risk-based lifecycle management.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset register

New infrastructure systems and significant changes to existing hardware, network or cloud architectures must undergo security assessment, risk treatment and authorisation or reauthorisation before production use.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology
The technology system is authorised to the highest security classification of the information and data it will process, store or communicate.
System authorisation must match the highest classification or data sensitivity handled by the infrastructure.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset register
Infrastructure systems must be authorised, engineered and operated for the highest classification and business impact level of information they process, store or communicate.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology

A register of the entity's authorised technology systems is developed, implemented and maintained, and includes the name and position of the Authorising Officer, system owner, date of authorisation, and any decisions to accept residual security risks.
An authorised system register creates traceability for infrastructure ownership, authorisation and accepted risk.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset register

NDIA must maintain a register of authorised infrastructure systems, including system owner, authorising officer, authorisation date, classification/BIL, residual risks and review/reauthorisation status.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology

Each technology system's suitability to be authorised to operate is reassessed when it undergoes significant functionality or architectural change, or where the system's security environment has changed considerably.
Major changes or changing threat conditions can invalidate previous authorisation decisions.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Technology lifecycle, authorisation and asset register
Infrastructure systems must be reassessed and, where required, reauthorised after significant functional, architectural, connectivity, hosting, control or threat-environment changes.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology
The TikTok application is prevented from being installed, and existing instances are removed, on government devices, unless a legitimate business reason exists.
Prohibited technology controls reduce data, device and Commonwealth security risks.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and managed endpoints; Networks and Cloud through access controls and app/service blocking.
NDIA must prevent installation and use of TikTok on government devices and remove detected instances unless a legitimate approved business reason exists.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology
The CSO or CISO approves any legitimate business reason for the use of the TikTok application on government devices and ensures specified mitigations are in place.
Exception governance is needed where prohibited technology is required for legitimate business use.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and managed endpoints; Networks and Cloud through exception monitoring and controls.
Any exception for TikTok use on NDIA government devices must be approved by the CSO or CISO, documented with mitigations, time limits and monitoring, and reviewed periodically.
Lifecycle management, authorisation, asset stocktake and controlled technology
The Australian Signals Directorate's temporary mitigations for legacy IT are applied to manage legacy information technology that cannot yet be replaced.
Legacy infrastructure can introduce unacceptable risk where replacement is delayed.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

Legacy hardware, network platforms, operating systems and cloud services that cannot be replaced must have ASD temporary mitigations, risk treatment plans, upgrade/replacement pathways and formal risk acceptance.
Facilities, security zones, racks, access controls and surveillance protection
Technology assets and their components, classified as SECRET or below are stored in the appropriate Security Zone based on their aggregated security classification or business impact level.
Classified technology assets need appropriate physical storage by aggregated classification or impact.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and network/security appliances; Cloud/Data Centre where NDIA manages physical components.
Secure facilities, security zones and physical protection of infrastructure
Technology assets and components classified SECRET or below must be stored in the appropriate Security Zone based on aggregated classification and business impact.
Facilities, security zones, racks, access controls and surveillance protection
Technology assets and their components classified as TOP SECRET are stored in suitable SCEC-endorsed racks or compartments within an accredited Security Zone Five area.
TOP SECRET technology assets require enhanced physical protection in accredited Zone Five facilities.
Conditional - applies where NDIA infrastructure handles TOP SECRET information, systems or components.
Secure facilities, security zones and physical protection of infrastructure
TOP SECRET technology assets must be stored only in suitable SCEC-endorsed racks or compartments within an accredited Security Zone Five area.
Cloud governance, HCF/IRAP assurance, data sovereignty, service levels and exit

Outsourced facilities that house technology assets and their components with a catastrophic business impact level are certified by ASIO T4 physical security and accredited by ASD before they are used operationally.
Catastrophic-impact outsourced facilities require specialist certification and accreditation before operation.
Conditional - applies to outsourced data centre or facility services housing catastrophic-BIL technology assets.
Cloud, data centre and hosting controls
NDIA must not use outsourced facilities for catastrophic-BIL technology assets until ASIO T4 certification and ASD accreditation requirements are met and recorded.
Commonwealth records, legal holds, retrieval, decommissioning and media sanitisation
Technology assets are disposed of securely in accordance with the Information Security Manual.
Secure disposal of technology assets prevents data leakage and uncontrolled asset re-use.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio and storage media; Cloud where provider-managed assets store NDIA data.
Secure information, media and technology asset disposal
Technology assets, components, media and provider-managed storage must be disposed of in accordance with the ISM and NDIA evidence requirements for sanitisation, destruction, transfer or return.
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls

A cyber security strategy and uplift plan is developed, implemented and maintained to manage the entity's cyber security risks in accordance with the ISM and the Guiding Principles to Embed a Zero Trust Culture.
A cyber strategy and uplift plan provides governance for improving infrastructure security and Zero Trust alignment.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups

NDIA infrastructure management must align with the cyber security strategy and uplift plan, ISM obligations and Zero Trust guiding principles, including measurable improvements and executive reporting.
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls
Patch applications mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory Essential Eight control to reduce compromise of infrastructure platforms, endpoints and cloud workloads.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must implement patch applications to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two for applications, consoles, agents, cloud workloads and endpoint software.
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls
Patch operating systems mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory Essential Eight control to reduce compromise of infrastructure platforms, endpoints and cloud workloads.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must implement patch operating systems to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two for servers, endpoints, network appliances and cloud infrastructure images.
MFA, least privilege, privileged administration, remote access and separation
Multi-factor authentication mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory Essential Eight control to reduce compromise of infrastructure platforms, endpoints and cloud workloads.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must implement multi-factor authentication to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two for users, administrators, remote access, cloud consoles and infrastructure management interfaces.
MFA, least privilege, privileged administration, remote access and separation
Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory Essential Eight control to reduce compromise of infrastructure platforms, endpoints and cloud workloads.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must implement restrict administrative privileges to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two for privileged access accounts, administration roles and infrastructure management functions.
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls
Application control mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory Essential Eight control to reduce compromise of infrastructure platforms, endpoints and cloud workloads.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must implement application control to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two for managed endpoints, servers and relevant infrastructure platforms.
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls
Restrict Microsoft Office macros mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory Essential Eight control to reduce macro-borne compromise of managed endpoints and cloud productivity services.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio/endpoints and SaaS productivity environments; supporting control for networks/cloud.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must restrict Microsoft Office macros to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two and prevent untrusted macro execution on managed devices and cloud productivity services.
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls
User application hardening mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Mandatory Essential Eight control to reduce compromise of infrastructure platforms, endpoints and cloud workloads.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must implement user application hardening to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two for managed devices, browsers, email clients and relevant cloud/SaaS user environments.
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls
Regular back-ups mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Backups are essential for resilience and recovery of infrastructure services and data.
Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage; Hardware and Networks for systems, configurations and logs.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must implement regular backups to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two, including backup coverage, protection, restoration testing and segregation from production compromise.
Cyber strategy, patching, hardening, backups and cryptographic controls

The remaining mitigation strategies from the Strategies to Mitigate Cyber Security Incidents are considered and, where required, implemented to achieve an acceptable level of residual risk for their entity.
Other ASD mitigation strategies may be needed to reach acceptable residual infrastructure risk.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.
Cyber security baseline, Essential Eight and backups
NDIA must assess ASD's other mitigation strategies for infrastructure environments and implement relevant controls where needed to reach accepted residual risk.
Gateway/SSE, Protective DNS, segmentation and security visibility
A Protective Domain Name System service or other security mechanisms is used to prevent connections to and from known malicious endpoints.
Protective DNS and equivalent controls reduce connection to known malicious infrastructure.
Directly applicable - Networks and cloud connectivity; Hardware Portfolio for managed endpoints.
Network security, gateways, DNS and secure service edge
NDIA must use Protective DNS or equivalent security mechanisms for internet-facing and outbound infrastructure traffic to block or detect connections to known malicious endpoints.
Cloud governance, HCF/IRAP assurance, data sovereignty, service levels and exit
Cloud Service Providers that have completed an IRAP assessment against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
IRAP-assessed cloud services provide assurance against the latest ISM controls before use.
Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage; Networks for cloud connectivity and Secure Service Edge services.
Cloud, data centre and hosting controls
NDIA must use Cloud Service Providers with an IRAP assessment against the latest ASD ISM within the previous 24 months for relevant cloud services and workloads.
Cloud governance, HCF/IRAP assurance, data sovereignty, service levels and exit
Entities consider IRAP assessment recommendations and findings, and implement on a risk-based approach.
IRAP findings must be treated, not just collected, for infrastructure risk decisions.
Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage, data centres, gateways and managed network services.
Cloud, data centre and hosting controls
NDIA must review IRAP recommendations and findings for cloud, data centre, gateway and managed services, risk-rate them, implement treatments and record accepted residual risks.
Cloud governance, HCF/IRAP assurance, data sovereignty, service levels and exit

Security classified or systems of government significance information and data is securely hosted using a Cloud Service Provider and Data Centre Provider that has been certified against the Australian Government Hosting Certification Framework.
Classified or Systems of Government Significance data requires certified hosting and data centre assurance.
Conditional - Cloud Compute and Storage and data centre hosting where information is security classified or declared SOGS.
Cloud, data centre and hosting controls

NDIA must host security classified or Systems of Government Significance information using Cloud Service Providers and Data Centre Providers certified under the Australian Government Hosting Certification Framework.
Cloud governance, HCF/IRAP assurance, data sovereignty, service levels and exit
The Data Centre Facilities Supplies Panel is used when procuring certified data centre space and services.
Use of the panel supports compliant procurement of certified data centre services.
Directly applicable - Cloud Compute and Storage/data centre services; Hardware and Networks for hosted infrastructure.
Cloud, data centre and hosting controls
When procuring certified data centre space or services, NDIA must use the Data Centre Facilities Supplies Panel unless an approved procurement exception applies.
Gateway/SSE, Protective DNS, segmentation and security visibility
Internet-connected technology systems, and the data they process, store or communicate, are protected by a gateway in accordance with the ISM and the Gateways Policy.
Gateways provide mandatory protection for internet-connected systems and their data flows.
Directly applicable - Networks and internet-connected hardware/cloud systems.
Network security, gateways, DNS and secure service edge
Internet-connected infrastructure and the data it processes, stores or communicates must be protected by an approved gateway or equivalent control in accordance with the ISM and Gateways Policy.
Gateway/SSE, Protective DNS, segmentation and security visibility
Gateways or Secure Service Edges that have completed an IRAP assessment (or ASD assessment for TOP SECRET gateways) against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
Gateway and Secure Service Edge assurance is needed because these services form the boundary between NDIA and external domains.
Directly applicable - Networks and cloud Secure Service Edge; conditional for TOP SECRET gateways.
Network security, gateways, DNS and secure service edge
NDIA must use gateways or Secure Service Edges that have current IRAP assessment, or ASD assessment for TOP SECRET gateways, against the latest ASD ISM within the previous 24 months.
Continuity, logging, vulnerability disclosure and ASD threat engagement
A vulnerability disclosure program and supporting processes and procedures are established to receive, verify, resolve and report on vulnerabilities disclosed by both internal and external sources.
Vulnerability disclosure supports early detection and remediation of externally reported weaknesses.
Directly applicable - internet-facing Networks and Cloud services; Hardware where externally reachable management interfaces exist.
Vulnerability management, disclosure and threat intelligence
NDIA must maintain a vulnerability disclosure program with defined intake, triage, verification, remediation, communication and reporting processes for infrastructure vulnerabilities.
MFA, least privilege, privileged administration, remote access and separation
Appropriate access to official information is enabled, including controlling access (including remote access) to supporting technology systems, networks, infrastructure, devices and applications.
Access controls are fundamental to protecting infrastructure and information.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

NDIA must control user, administrator and remote access to infrastructure systems, networks, devices, applications and information using least privilege, authentication, authorisation, monitoring and periodic review.
MFA, least privilege, privileged administration, remote access and separation
Approval for remote access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems in international locations is only granted if approved by the Australian Signals Directorate.
International remote access to TOP SECRET systems presents heightened risk and needs ASD approval.
Conditional - applies only where NDIA permits international remote access to TOP SECRET systems or data.
NDIA must not approve remote access to TOP SECRET information, data or systems from international locations unless ASD approval is obtained and recorded.
MFA, least privilege, privileged administration, remote access and separation
A security risk assessment of the proposed location and work environment informs decisions to allow personnel to work remotely in international locations.
Remote work location risks can affect NDIA infrastructure and information confidentiality.
Directly applicable - remote administration/access to Networks, Cloud and managed devices from international locations.
Before allowing international remote work or administration, NDIA must complete a security risk assessment of the proposed location, work environment, connectivity and device controls.
MFA, least privilege, privileged administration, remote access and separation

Personnel are not granted approval to work remotely in locations where Australian Government information or resources are exposed to extrajudicial directions from a foreign government that conflict with Australian law, unless operationally required.
Foreign legal or coercive access risks can conflict with Australian law and expose government information.
Conditional - applies to international remote work or administration involving NDIA infrastructure or information resources.

NDIA must not approve remote work or infrastructure access from locations where government information or resources may be exposed to conflicting extrajudicial foreign directions, unless operationally required and risk-approved.
MFA, least privilege, privileged administration, remote access and separation
Separating personnel have their access to Australian Government resources withdrawn upon separation or transfer from the entity.
Separation controls prevent former or transferred personnel retaining access to infrastructure and data.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, Networks, and Cloud Compute and Storage.

NDIA must promptly withdraw or transfer access to infrastructure platforms, privileged accounts, devices, tokens, cloud consoles, network administration tools and physical facilities when personnel separate or transfer.
Facilities, security zones, racks, access controls and surveillance protection
Protective security is integrated in the process of planning, selecting, designing and modifying entity facilities for the protection of people, information and resources.
Physical security planning must be integrated when selecting or modifying infrastructure facilities.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.
Secure facilities, security zones and physical protection of infrastructure
NDIA must integrate protective security into planning, selecting, designing and modifying facilities that house ICT hardware, network services, storage media or supporting infrastructure.
Facilities, security zones, racks, access controls and surveillance protection
A facility security plan is developed for new facilities, facilities under construction or major refurbishments of existing facilities.
Facility security plans define protections for new or refurbished infrastructure locations.
Directly applicable - Hardware Portfolio, network rooms, data centres and physical spaces supporting cloud or managed infrastructure.
